text: Meridian Specialty Lending is a fictional mid-size lender that takes card payments, holds applicants' financial data, and needs a clean SOC 2 report before its next funding round. Its CISO has one mandate: design the security architecture this regulated company actually needs, using SABSA's discipline from Chapter 2 and the layered-defense thinking from Chapter 1, instead of a generic checklist.

Step one is the Business Attributes Profile, built with real stakeholders before any technology gets named: regulatory standing, investor confidence, operational resilience, and cost discipline. Every decision made for the rest of this lab has to trace back to one of those four rows, or it doesn't belong in the architecture yet.

Those attributes get translated into a conceptual strategy, then into six concrete defense-in-depth layers. A segmented cardholder-data environment and tokenized intake shrink what regulatory standing actually has to cover. Hardware-key MFA, EDR, and SIEM correlation protect operational resilience. Every layer in this lab gets written down with the specific attribute it serves.

The layer most likely to get cut in a budget review is tokenization, so this lab writes the actual business case for it: removing raw card numbers from everything downstream of intake shrinks the compliance boundary, which lowers audit cost and ongoing security spend at the same time -- one decision satisfying two business attributes at once.

The lab closes with a one-page architecture decision record: the decision, the business driver it serves, the alternative that was considered, and why that alternative was rejected. That's a real artifact, ready to feed directly into Meridian's GRC program, not just a classroom exercise.

This lab proved the actual difference between an architect and an engineer from Lesson 1: deciding which controls a business needs, and justifying that decision in business terms. Lesson 30 picks up these same risks and makes them quantitative, mapping every control to several compliance frameworks at once.
